what: Constellation Energy is the largest producer of carbon-free electricity in the United States. It owns the biggest fleet of nuclear power stations in the country and sells that power to businesses, utilities and, increasingly, data centre operators.
customers: Large commercial and industrial users, utilities, and retail electricity customers; increasingly technology companies buying power for data centres.
money: electricity from nuclear, plus some gas, hydro, wind and solar
selling electricity and gas to businesses and households
moat: Nuclear plants that cannot be replicated: new ones take a decade or more to licence and build, while its existing fleet produces round-the-clock carbon-free power.
risks: Power prices are set by markets it does not control
Nuclear plants carry operational and regulatory risk, and an outage is expensive
Federal support such as production tax credits can change
It paid a high price for the Calpine acquisition and took on debt
opportunities: Data centre operators are signing long-term contracts for carbon-free power at premium prices
Nuclear output is valued more highly as clean, always-on electricity becomes scarce
Licence extensions and uprates add output with little new capital
watch: New long-term power agreements with data centre customers and the prices in them.
